inputs.goal:
Map E. coli sequencing reads from samples A, B, and C to the reference genome,
sort and index the resulting alignments, then call genomic variants across all
three samples jointly. The reference genome and reads are in the INPUT_DIR.
Write all outputs to WORK_DIR.

Map E. coli sequencing reads from samples A, B, and C to the reference genome,
sort and index the resulting alignments, then call genomic variants across all
three samples jointly. The reference genome and reads are in the INPUT_DIR.
Write all outputs to WORK_DIR.

work_dir_structure.input: WORK_DIR/input/  — staged input data (read-only, do not write here)
work_dir_structure.steps: WORK_DIR/steps/  — one subdirectory per executed step (NN_rulename/)
work_dir_structure.logs: WORK_DIR/logs/   — per-rule log files written automatically
work_dir_structure.snakefile: WORK_DIR/Snakefile — accumulating workflow, appended each step

path_conventions.input_files: Relative to WORK_DIR/input/. Example: 'samples/A.fastq' resolves to WORK_DIR/input/samples/A.fastq
path_conventions.output_files: Relative to this step's directory. Example: 'A.bam' resolves to WORK_DIR/steps/NN_rulename/A.bam
path_conventions.chained_inputs: To use a prior step's output as input, prefix with 'steps/NN_rulename/'. Example: 'steps/01_bwa_mem_A/A.bam'
path_conventions.never_use: Absolute paths, environment variable names, or bare filenames without the correct prefix.

results.name: bazam
results.description: Bazam is a smarter way to realign reads from one genome to another. If you've tried to use Picard SAMtoFASTQ or samtools bam2fq before and ended up unsatisfied with complicated, long running inefficient pipelines, bazam might be what you wanted. Bazam will output FASTQ in a form that can stream directly into common aligners such as BWA or Bowtie2, so that you can quickly and easily realign reads without extraction to any intermediate format. Bazam can target a specific region of the genome, specified as a region or a gene name if you prefer.

results.name: ngs-disambiguate
results.description:
Disambiguation algorithm for reads aligned to two species (e.g. human
and mouse genomes) from Tophat, Hisat2, STAR or BWA mem.

results.name: bwa aln
results.description: Map reads with bwa aln. For more information about BWA see `BWA documentation <http://bio-bwa.sourceforge.net/bwa.shtml>`_.

results.name: bwa mem samblaster
results.description: Map reads using bwa mem, mark duplicates by samblaster and sort and index by sambamba.

results.name: bwa sampe
results.description: Map paired-end reads with bwa sampe. For more information about BWA see `BWA documentation <http://bio-bwa.sourceforge.net/bwa.shtml>`_.

results.name: bwa index
results.description: Creates a BWA index.

results.name: bwa mem
results.description: Map reads using bwa mem, with optional sorting using samtools or picard.

results.name: bwa sam(se/pe)
results.description: Map paired-end reads with either bwa samse or sampe.

results.name: bwa samse
results.description: Map single-end reads with bwa samse. For more information about BWA see `BWA documentation <http://bio-bwa.sourceforge.net/bwa.shtml>`_.

results.name: bwa-mem2 index
results.description: Creates a bwa-mem, bwa-mem2 or bwa-meme index.

results.name: bwa-memx
results.description: Collection of bwa-mem, bwa-mem2 and bwa-meme.

results.name: bwa-mem2 index
results.description: Creates a bwa-meme index.

results.name: bwa-meme
results.description: BWA-MEME is a practical and efficient seeding algorithm based on a suffix array search algorithm that solves the challenges in utilizing learned indices for SMEM search which is extensively used in the seeding phase. It achieves up to 3.45× speedup in seeding throughput over BWA-MEM2 by reducing the number of instructions by 4.60×, memory accesses by 8.77× and LLC misses by 2.21×, while ensuring the identical SAM output to BWA-MEM2.

results.name: samtools fixmate
results.description: Use samtools to correct mate information after BWA mapping.

results.name: bwa-meth index
results.description: Index a reference sequence for future BS-Seq mapping.

results.name: bwa-meth memx
results.description: Align BS-Seq reads on an indexed reference

results.name: bwa mem samblaster
results.description: Map reads using bwa-mem2, mark duplicates by samblaster and sort and index by sambamba.

results.name: bwa-mem2 index
results.description: Creates a bwa-mem2 index.

results.name: bwa-mem2
results.description: Bwa-mem2 is the next version of the bwa-mem algorithm in bwa. It produces alignment identical to bwa and is ~1.3-3.1x faster depending on the use-case, dataset and the running machine. Optional sorting using samtools or picard.

results.name: bwa_mapping
results.description: Map reads with bwa-mem and index with samtools index

outputs.name: bwa mem
outputs.description: Map reads using bwa mem, with optional sorting using samtools or picard.
outputs.example_rule:
rule bwa_mem:
    input:
        reads=["reads/{sample}.1.fastq", "reads/{sample}.2.fastq"],
        idx=multiext("genome", ".amb", ".ann", ".bwt", ".pac", ".sa"),
    output:
        "mapped/{sample}.bam",
    log:
        "logs/bwa_mem/{sample}.log",
    params:
        extra=r"-R '@RG\tID:{sample}\tSM:{sample}'",
        sorting="none",  # Can be 'none', 'samtools' or 'picard'.
        sort_order="queryname",  # Can be 'queryname' or 'coordinate'.
        sort_extra="",  # Extra args for samtools/picard.
    threads: 8
    wrapper:
        "master/bio/bwa/mem"

outputs.name: bcftools call
outputs.example_rule:
rule bcftools_call:
    input:
        pileup="{sample}.pileup.bcf",
    output:
        calls="{sample}.calls.bcf",
    params:
        uncompressed_bcf=False,
        caller="-m",  # valid options include -c/--consensus-caller or -m/--multiallelic-caller
        extra="--ploidy 1 --prior 0.001",
    log:
        "logs/bcftools_call/{sample}.log",
    wrapper:
        "master/bio/bcftools/call"

outputs.name: bcftools mpileup
outputs.description: Generate VCF or BCF containing genotype likelihoods for one or multiple alignment (BAM or CRAM) files.
outputs.example_rule:
rule bcftools_mpileup:
    input:
        alignments=["mapped/{sample}.bam", "mapped/{sample}.bam"],
        ref="genome.fasta",  # this can be left out if --no-reference is in options
        index="genome.fasta.fai",
    output:
        pileup="pileups/{sample}.pileup.bcf",
    params:
        uncompressed_bcf=False,
        extra="--max-depth 100 --min-BQ 15",
    log:
        "logs/bcftools_mpileup/{sample}.log",
    wrapper:
        "master/bio/bcftools/mpileup"
